items.title: Neal Caine interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019
items.q: I have a sax player who I love who plays in my band sometimes, Stephen Riley.

ctx.x: Yeah. And then you have to — not have to — and then you get people to play it and what actually comes out may or may not be what you had sort of envisioned. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

That’s right. That’s right. A lot of times it’s not. Sometimes it is, usually it’s not. And sometimes it’s better than you thought, and sometimes it’s worse. And like you know I have a sax player who I love who plays in my band sometimes, Stephen Riley. And I’ll write like a song with the harmony. And he usually only plays what I write half the time. And sometimes he just does his own thing. And that usually sometimes sounds a lot better. You know I like to keep it open, you know, because you never know what…

When you’re writing for two tenors, are you like sort of methodical, like all right I’m playing a G sus type bass line and I’m going to give this tenor the third, and this tenor the fifth, or is it a little more just what sounds right. I don’t know if that was a —
